rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an aging heat treatment to form L1₀ precipitates, while the paper uses rapid quenching to stabilize a dual-phase fcc + C14 Laves microstructure. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies an inert-atmosphere aging at 500–600°C and room-temperature magnetic measurements, whereas the paper uses arc melting on a water-cooled Cu hearth and magnetic measurements up to 400 K. The processing and measurement regimes are different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes domain wall pinning by coherent L1₀ precipitates. The paper's mechanism involves antiferromagnetic coupling between sublattices, orbital moment contributions, and spin-canted components at fcc/C14 interfaces. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: Both predict an increase in coercivity above ~100 Oe, but the hypothesis does not specify the magnitude or the multiple magnetic transitions observed in the paper. The agreement is limited to the general direction of the property change.
